entities.summary:
The Haitian Revolution was a pivotal 1791-1804 slave revolt that took place in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, which is now Haiti, under the leadership of Toussaint Louverture and Jean-Jacques Dessalines. It was a significant event in the arc of world history, as it led to the establishment of Haiti as the first independent black nation in the world. The revolution was sparked by the brutal treatment of enslaved Africans, who comprised the majority of the colony's population, and was fueled by the ideals of the French Revolution.

The revolution began in August 1791, when a group of enslaved Africans, led by Boukman Dutty, staged a successful revolt against their French colonial masters. Over the next several years, the rebels, who were primarily black, fought against the French army and their allies, including the Spanish and the British. In 1804, the rebels, led by Dessalines, declared Haiti's independence, marking the end of French rule and the beginning of a new era in Haitian history.

The Haitian Revolution had significant consequences for the world. It led to the abolition of slavery in Haiti and paved the way for the abolition of slavery in other parts of the world. It also inspired other slave revolts and movements for independence in the Americas and beyond. The revolution's impact can be seen in the rise of African diasporic cultures and the growing awareness of the injustices of slavery and colonialism.

One of the most enduring legacies of the Haitian Revolution is its impact on the global struggle for human rights. As the first successful slave revolt in modern history, it showed that enslaved people were capable of fighting back against their oppressors and achieving freedom. This legacy continues to inspire social justice movements around the world today.
